title: PreBit -- A multimodal model with Twitter FinBERT embeddings for extreme price movement prediction of Bitcoin

extraction.methodology_summary: The paper proposes a multimodal model called PreBit, combining a Support Vector Machine (SVM) model trained on technical analysis (TA) features and correlated asset prices with a text-based Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) trained on sentence-level FinBERT embeddings of daily Bitcoin-related tweets. The prediction probabilities from the Twitter and TA models are fused using an SVM classifier to output a joint prediction for extreme price movements (up or down by 2% or 5%). The models are evaluated through an ablation study on test data from June 2020 to May 2021, and the resulting signals are backtested on a simple long-only trading strategy.
extraction.universe: Bitcoin (BTC), including correlated assets Ethereum and Gold, and daily Twitter posts containing the keyword 'Bitcoin'

key_findings: Integrating Twitter content via FinBERT embeddings improves predictive performance for upward extreme price movements of Bitcoin compared to using price-based technical indicators alone.
Multimodal Fusion models outperform individual modality models in F1-score and accuracy for tasks predicting upward price spikes.
Trading strategies built upon the proposed model signals significantly reduce maximum drawdown compared to a Buy and Hold strategy while capturing profitable opportunities.
During bear market periods, the proposed trading strategies achieve positive returns (e.g., 32% profit for TA SVM) while the underlying benchmark asset price drops significantly.
limitations: The evaluation and backtest are performed on a limited period in time (one year), which may not generalize across all market cycles due to asset non-stationarity.
The collected tweet sample size (5,000 tweets per day) may not fully capture the entire market sentiment or the specific impact of major crypto influencers.
Transaction costs, slippage, and liquidity constraints are omitted in the naive backtesting framework.
